item.title: Brisk 0.7.2
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • Changing the default refresh interval in Settings > Refresh now takes effect right away. Previously, the new interval only applied after each subscription's next scheduled refresh, so shortening it from 15 to 5 minutes could still wait up to 15 minutes.

item.title: Brisk 0.7.1
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • The article header now shows the site icon next to the feed name.

item.title: Brisk 0.7.0
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • New "Today" smart list in the sidebar shows articles published since midnight. It can also be chosen in widgets.
  • The article list now shows a small picture for each article, taken from the feed or the first image in the article. Only visible rows are loaded. You can turn this off in Settings > List.
  • New option in Settings > List: mark articles as read when you scroll past them.
  • Quiet hours: in Settings > Notifications, choose a time range when Brisk won't send new-article notifications. Articles are still downloaded.
  • The menu bar icon is larger and easier to see.

item.title: Brisk 0.6.4
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • Subscriptions now show their site icons in the sidebar and next to the feed name in the article list. Subscriptions with notifications turned on show a small bell next to their name.
  • Search is faster and more accurate. It no longer matches text hidden inside HTML markup, such as link addresses or style names, and it still finds parts of words.
  • After updating, articles you already have are added to the search index in the background. Until that finishes, some older articles may not appear in search results.

item.title: Brisk 0.6.3
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • Brisk no longer becomes unresponsive with large numbers of articles. The article list now loads 300 articles at a time and loads more as you scroll, so marking articles as read, searching, and switching lists stay responsive.
  • Mark All as Read, deleting subscriptions or folders, resetting articles, and importing OPML now run in the background. If an operation takes longer than a moment, a progress indicator appears at the bottom of the article list.
  • While searching, Mark All as Read now applies to every matching article, not only the ones loaded in the list.
  • The article count next to the list title always shows the total number of articles.

item.title: Brisk 0.6.2
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • Select multiple folders and subscriptions in the sidebar with Command-click or Shift-click. The article list shows articles from everything selected, and search and Mark All as Read apply to the selection.
  • Drag several subscriptions or folders at once. When multiple items are dragged, the first item is shown with a "+N" badge.
  • OPML export and import now preserve empty folders, sidebar order, custom names, and per-feed settings such as notifications, full text, translation, check interval, and retention. OPML files from other apps still import as before.
  • When adding a subscription, you can edit its name before saving.
  • Toolbar and floating action icons now show their names as tooltips.

item.title: Brisk 0.6.1
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • Language setting: Brisk is now available in Korean and English. Korean remains the default. To change the language, open Settings > General > Language; Brisk restarts to apply it.
  • Widgets show their content in the selected language.
  • The disk image now includes English installation instructions.

item.title: Brisk 0.6.0
item.description:
Requires a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) and macOS 14 or later.

  • In-app updates: Brisk checks for new versions once a day and installs them on request (Check for Updates in the menu)
  • Keyboard focus moves between the sidebar, article list, and article view with the Left and Right arrow keys; Up and Down scroll the article view
  • Search within the current list (Command-F), per-feed notification toggle, and list actions that are always visible
  • Folders and subscriptions can be reordered and moved by dragging in the sidebar
  • Improved full-text retrieval, plus refresh and memory performance improvements

Earlier versions do not include the updater. Install this version manually once; later versions will be delivered automatically.
